method: Direct operator reading of NASA primary educational material and the NASA-hosted SpaceX Falcon launch/landing infographic; not a third Parallel dispatch.

sources.title: NASA Basics of Space Flight — Gravity & Mechanics
NASA-hosted SpaceX Falcon 9 launch and landing sequence

claims.text: An object slows when its acceleration points opposite its motion; an applied force can produce that acceleration.
A rocket produces thrust by expelling mass through a nozzle; the vehicle accelerates in the opposite direction.
Chemical rocket combustion heats gas that expands through the nozzle. Rockets carry fuel and oxidizer, and their propulsion expels part of their onboard mass.
The Falcon 9 flight sequence published by NASA shows an entry burn in which the first-stage engines restart to slow the stage.
In the published Falcon 9 descent sequence, grid fins guide the stage aerodynamically, and a final engine ignition brings it to a soft vertical landing.
In a powered vertical descent, downward exhaust provides upward thrust that can reduce the booster's downward speed. This braking uses propellant even though the vehicle is moving downward.

interpretation.operator-claim-landing-mechanism: Operator synthesis of the cited opposite-force/exhaust principle and documented powered landing; no numerical thrust, speed or timing inference.

limitations: The sequence is illustrative and mission-specific; do not infer universal burn counts, burn durations, hover behavior, precise engine counts or an exhaust heat shield. The earlier forum-based atmosphere claim is retained as uncertain, not primary evidence.
